questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the names of States and Union Territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **First Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** contains the list of all **States** and **Union Territories** that comprise the **Indian Union**.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with the official language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XVII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVII** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the **Official Language** of the country, encompassing **Articles 343 to 351**.
 
• According to **Article 343**, the official language of the **Union** is **Hindi** written in the **Devanagari script**, although the use of **English** was permitted for official purposes for an initial period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• The provisions are categorized into four distinct chapters: **Language of the Union** (Articles 343-344), **Regional Languages** (Articles 345-347), **Language of the Supreme Court and High Courts** (Articles 348-349), and **Special Directives** (Articles 350-351).
 
• **Article 351** specifically directs the Union to promote the spread of the **Hindi language** and to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of **India**.
 
• The **Official Languages Act of 1963** was subsequently enacted to provide for the continued use of **English** for official purposes of the Union and for use in **Parliament** even after the 15-year period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XV**:

 
 
• This part pertains to **Elections** and includes **Articles 324 to 329**.
 
• It establishes the **Election Commission of India**, which is responsible for the direction and control of **Parliamentary** and **State Legislative** elections.
 
 
 
• **Part XVI**:
 
 
• It contains **Special Provisions** relating to certain classes, covering **Articles 330 to 342**.
 
• These provisions ensure the representation and protection of interests for **Scheduled Castes**, **Scheduled Tribes**, and other backward classes.
 
 
 
• **Part XVIII**:
 
 
• This section covers **Emergency Provisions** under **Articles 352 to 360**.
 
• It empowers the **President of India** to declare a **National Emergency**, **State Emergency (President’s Rule)**, or **Financial Emergency**.

questions.question: Which physical property remains the same on both Earth and the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is defined as the fundamental measure of the total amount of **matter** contained within a physical body or object.
 
• It is an **intrinsic property** of an object, which means it remains constant regardless of the object's location in the universe, whether it is on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or in a state of **weightlessness** in outer space.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**, and it is measured using a **beam balance**, which compares an unknown mass with a known standard mass.
 
• According to **Newton's laws of motion**, mass is a quantitative measure of **inertia**, representing the resistance offered by an object to any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
 
• Since the quantity of **atoms** and **molecules** within a solid body does not change when moved from one **gravitational field** to another, the **mass** remains identical on both the **Earth** and the **Moon**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight**:

 
 
• Unlike mass, **weight** is a **vector quantity** representing the **gravitational force** acting on an object.
 
• It is calculated by the formula **W = m × g**, where 'm' is mass and 'g' is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• Because the Moon's gravity is roughly **1/6th** (approximately **16.6%**) of Earth's gravity, an object will weigh much less on the Moon than on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration**:
 
 
• This refers to the **acceleration** of an object caused by the force of **gravitation**.
 
• On **Earth**, the standard value of 'g' is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, while on the **Moon**, it is only **1.62 m/s²** due to the Moon having a smaller **mass** and **radius**.
 
 
 
• **Pressure**:
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** exerted per unit **area** (**P = F/A**).
 
• Since the weight (force) of an object changes depending on the **local gravity**, the pressure it exerts on a surface will also differ between the Earth and the Moon.

questions.question: Who was William Wordsworth's collaborator in the publication of "Lyrical Ballads"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samuel Taylor Coleridge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lyrical Ballads**, with a Few Other Poems, is a seminal collection first published in **1798**, marking the official beginning of the **Romantic Movement** in **English Literature**.
 
• The work was a landmark collaboration between **William Wordsworth** and **Samuel Taylor Coleridge**, who sought to break away from the rigid, formal structures of 18th-century **Neoclassical poetry**.
 
• The poets established a unique division of labor: **Wordsworth** aimed to provide a fresh perspective on **ordinary life** and **common incidents**, while **Coleridge** focused on **supernatural** elements and making them appear **psychologically credible**.
 
• **Coleridge's** primary contribution to the 1798 edition was the lengthy and iconic poem **The Rime of the Ancient Mariner**, which stands as a masterpiece of **imagination** and **symbolism**.
 
• In the second edition published in **1800**, **Wordsworth** added a famous **Preface** that outlined their poetic manifesto, advocating for the use of the **language of men** rather than elevated **poetic diction**.
 
• The collection also featured **Wordsworth's** **Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey**, which serves as a foundational text for **Pantheism** and nature-oriented philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samuel Taylor Coleridge**:

 
 
• A founder of the **Romantic Movement** and a member of the **Lake Poets**, he is well known for his prose work **Biographia Literaria**.
 
• His unfinished poems **Kubla Khan** and **Christabel** are celebrated for their **Gothic** atmosphere and exploration of the **subconscious**.
 
 
 
• **Robert Southey**:
 
 
• The third major member of the **Lake Poets** along with Wordsworth and Coleridge, he served as the **Poet Laureate** from 1813 to 1843.
 
 
 
• **Percy Bysshe Shelley**:
 
 
• A **Second-Generation Romantic** poet, he was known for his radical politics and lyrical masterpieces like **Prometheus Unbound** and **Ode to the West Wind**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Byron**:
 
 
• Another **Second-Generation Romantic**, famous for creating the **Byronic Hero** and writing the epic satire **Don Juan**.

questions.question: In which Olympic Games was the present Olympic flag first hoisted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1920 Summer Olympics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Olympic flag** was designed and created by **Baron Pierre de Coubertin**, the founder of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**, in **1913**.
 
• The flag made its official debut and was first hoisted during the **1920 Summer Olympics**, also known as the **Games of the VII Olympiad**, held in **Antwerp, Belgium**.
 
• Although the flag was presented at the **Olympic Congress** in **Paris** in **1914** to mark the **20th anniversary** of the **Olympic Movement**, the **outbreak of World War I** prevented its use in the cancelled 1916 Games.
 
• The **Antwerp Games** represented a symbolic moment of **global peace** and **unity** following the devastation of the **Great War**, making the introduction of the flag highly significant.
 
• The original flag hoisted in **Antwerp** remained the official flag for the **Summer Games** for **68 years** until it was replaced by a new flag at the **1988 Seoul Olympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symbolism of the Olympic Flag:**

 
 
• It features **five interlaced rings** of **blue, yellow, black, green, and red** on a **white background**, representing the **five inhabited continents**: **Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania**.
 
• **Pierre de Coubertin** chose these colors because every **national flag** in the world at that time contained at least one of these **six colors** (including the white base).
 
 
 
• **1924 Summer Olympics (Paris):**
 
 
• These Games were notable for introducing the **Olympic motto**: **Citius, Altius, Fortius** (Faster, Higher, Stronger).
 
• They also established the tradition of raising **three flags** at the closing ceremony: the **IOC flag**, the **host country flag**, and the **next host country flag**.
 
 
 
• **1924 Winter Olympics (Chamonix):**
 
 
• This was the **inaugural Winter Olympic Games**, originally called **International Winter Sports Week**.
 
• Prior to **1924**, winter sports like **Figure Skating** and **Ice Hockey** were occasionally included in the **Summer Olympics** schedule.
 
 
 
• **Other Antwerp Firsts:**
 
 
• The **Olympic Oath** was first taken by athletes in **1920**, and the **release of doves** as a symbol of peace was also introduced during the opening ceremony.

questions.question: Which hormone inhibits plant growth and can cause wilting of leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abscisic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abscisic acid (ABA)** is a specialized **plant growth inhibitor** that regulates various physiological processes, primarily acting as a **stress hormone**.
 
• It inhibits **plant growth** and metabolism, serving as an antagonist to growth-promoting hormones like **Auxins** and **Gibberellins**.
 
• One of its most significant effects is inducing the **closure of stomata** in the leaf epidermis during water stress; this reduces **transpiration** but also results in the **wilting of leaves**.
 
• ABA is responsible for the **abscission** of leaves, fruits, and flowers by promoting the development of the **abscission layer** at the base of the plant organs.
 
• It plays a vital role in **seed development** and **maturation** by inducing **seed dormancy**, ensuring that seeds do not germinate until environmental conditions are favorable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Auxin**:

 
 
• Primarily synthesized at the **shoot and root tips**, it promotes **cell elongation** and **apical dominance**.
 
• It is involved in **phototropism**, causing the plant to grow toward light sources.
 
 
 
• **Gibberellins**:
 
 
• These hormones promote **stem elongation**, **bolting** (sudden stalk growth), and the breaking of **seed dormancy**.
 
• They are widely used in agriculture to increase the size of fruits like **grapes** and to speed up the **malting process** in the brewing industry.
 
 
 
• **Cytokinin**:
 
 
• Essential for **cell division** (cytokinesis), these hormones are found in high concentrations in regions of rapid growth such as **root apices** and **developing shoots**.
 
• They help delay **leaf senescence** and promote the formation of **chloroplasts**.

questions.question: When was the "four-quarter" format introduced in international hockey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** officially transitioned international hockey matches from two halves of **35 minutes** each to a **four-quarter** format on **September 1, 2014**.
 
• Under this regulation, a standard match duration was reduced from 70 minutes to **60 minutes**, comprising four periods of **15 minutes** each.
 
• The implementation of this format was designed to improve the **flow and intensity** of the game while providing more opportunities for analysis and commercial breaks.
 
• A significant feature introduced alongside this format was the mandatory **40-second time-out** following the award of a **penalty corner** and the scoring of a **goal**, ensuring the clock is stopped during these set-piece situations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Structure of Intervals:
 
 
• A **two-minute break** is provided between the first and second quarters, as well as between the third and fourth quarters.
 
• The **halftime interval** between the second and third quarters is maintained at **ten minutes**.
 
 
 
• Purpose and Impact:
 
 
• The **FIH** aimed to make the sport more **television-friendly** and appealing to global audiences by aligning it with the formats of other high-paced professional sports.
 
• The format allows teams to maintain **higher physical intensity** throughout the match due to the frequent short breaks, which facilitates better player recovery and strategic rotations.
 
• Major tournaments like the **Champions Trophy** held in late **2014** were among the first elite competitions to showcase this updated timing structure.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly reflects triathlon events?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swim, Cycle, Run**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Triathlon** is an endurance multisport race consisting of three distinct disciplines performed sequentially without a significant break between them.
 
• The standard and internationally recognized sequence for a triathlon is **Swimming**, followed by **Cycling**, and concluding with **Running**. This order is strictly maintained by governing bodies like **World Triathlon**.
 
• The **Swim** leg is placed first primarily for safety reasons; athletes are at their freshest at the start, reducing the risk of **exhaustion-related accidents** or drowning in open water.
 
• The **Cycling** leg follows the swim, allowing athletes to utilize a different set of muscle groups while the heart rate settles into a steady rhythm after the horizontal position of swimming.
 
• The **Run** leg serves as the final segment because it is the most physically taxing on the joints due to high-impact movements, and finishing with a run ensures that athletes can safely cross the **finish line** even if they are heavily fatigued.
 
• Efficiency in these events is often determined by **Transitions**, which are the timed intervals spent changing gear between the sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transition Phases**:

 
 
• **T1 (Transition 1)**: Occurs between the **Swim** and the **Cycle**, where athletes remove wetsuits and put on helmets and cycling shoes.
 
• **T2 (Transition 2)**: Occurs between the **Cycle** and the **Run**, where athletes switch from cycling shoes to running shoes.
 
 
 
• **Standard Race Distances**:
 
 
• **Olympic/Standard Distance**: Comprises a **1.5 km swim**, a **40 km bike ride**, and a **10 km run**.
 
• **Sprint Distance**: Usually half the Olympic distance, involving a **750 m swim**, **20 km bike**, and **5 km run**.
 
• **Ironman Triathlon**: One of the most difficult one-day sporting events, consisting of a **3.8 km swim**, a **180 km bike**, and a full marathon of **42.2 km**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: The modern version of the sport is widely attributed to the **San Diego Track Club**, which held the first official triathlon in **1974** at **Mission Bay, California**.

questions.question: When was NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)** was established on **July 12, 1982**, to promote sustainable and equitable agriculture and rural development.
 
• It was created through the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act 1981**, following the specific recommendations of the **B. Sivaraman Committee**, also known as the **CRAFICARD** (Committee to Review Arrangements For Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development).
 
• **NABARD** replaced three major entities: the **Agricultural Credit Department (ACD)**, the **Rural Planning and Credit Cell (RPCC)** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, and the **Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC)**.
 
• The institution was formally dedicated to the nation by the then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** on **November 5, 1982**, with an initial paid-up capital of **100 crore**.
 
• It acts as the **apex regulatory body** for the overall regulation and licensing of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)** and apex **cooperative banks** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organizational Structure and Governance**:

 
 
• **Headquarters**: The bank is headquartered in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**, and operates through several regional offices across the country.
 
• **Ownership**: While it was initially a joint venture between the **RBI** and the **Government of India**, the government now holds **100 percent equity** in the bank.
 
 
 
• **Primary Functions and Initiatives**:
 
 
• **Refinance**: Provides long-term and short-term **refinance** to various financial institutions to promote investment in rural areas.
 
• **Financial Inclusion**: Instrumental in the development of the **Self-Help Group (SHG) Bank Linkage Project** and the design of the **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)** scheme in **1998**.
 
• **Funds**: Manages the **Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)**, which assists state governments in completing ongoing rural infrastructure projects.

questions.question: The 'Jeevan Pramaan' initiative is associated with:

options.text: Offering skill development training for youth
Issuing digital life certificates for pensioners

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Issuing digital life certificates for pensioners**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jeevan Pramaan** is a biometric-enabled **Digital Life Certificate** (DLC) for pensioners, designed to streamline the process of proving one is alive to continue receiving pension benefits.
 
• The initiative addresses the requirement for pensioners to submit a **Life Certificate** (Pramaan Patra) every year in November to their **Pension Disbursing Agency**.
 
• It utilizes **Aadhaar-based biometric authentication**, allowing pensioners to verify their identity through **fingerprints** or **iris recognition** without physical visits to banks or post offices.
 
• The digital certificate is stored in a centralized **Life Certificate Repository**, making it instantly accessible to **Pension Disbursing Agencies** (PDAs) like **Banks** and **Treasuries**.
 
• This system promotes **Ease of Living** for senior citizens, especially those who are physically infirm or reside far from their disbursing branches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Launch and Administration:
 
 
• Launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **November 10, 2014**, as part of the **Digital India** vision.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology** (MeitY).
 
 
 
• Eligibility and Usage:
 
 
• Applicable to retired employees of the **Central Government**, **State Governments**, **Railway**, **Defense**, and other government bodies.
 
• Pensioners can generate the certificate using the **Jeevan Pramaan** mobile app, **Common Service Centres (CSCs)**, or specialized biometric devices at home.
 
 
 
• Technological Impact:
 
 
• As of recent data, over **1 crore** digital life certificates have been successfully processed, significantly reducing identity fraud and administrative delays.
 
• A unique **Jeevan Pramaan ID** is generated for each transaction, serving as a permanent reference for the pensioner.

questions.question: Which country has been India's largest trading partner most recently?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People's Republic of China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the data from the **Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI)** and the **Ministry of Commerce**, the **People's Republic of China** emerged as **India's largest trading partner** in the fiscal year **2023-24**.
 
• The total **bilateral trade** between India and China reached **$118.4 billion**, marginally exceeding the trade volume with the **United States**.
 
• India's **exports** to China saw a growth of **8.7%**, amounting to **$16.67 billion**, driven by sectors like **iron ore**, **cotton yarn**, and **handloom products**.
 
• India's **imports** from China increased by **3.24%** to reach **$101.7 billion**, resulting in a **trade deficit** of **$85 billion**.
 
• Major items imported from China include **telecom instruments**, **computer hardware**, **electronic components**, and **pharmaceutical intermediates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United States of America**:

 
 
• The **USA** was India's top trading partner in **2021-22** and **2022-23**.
 
• In **2023-24**, bilateral trade with the USA stood at **$118.3 billion**, dropping from **$128.55 billion** in the previous fiscal year.
 
 
 
• **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**:
 
 
• The **UAE** remains India's **third-largest** trading partner with a trade volume of **$83.6 billion** in **2023-24**.
 
• Trade is supported by the **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)** signed in **2022**.
 
 
 
• **Japan**:
 
 
• Japan is a crucial strategic and economic partner, though its total trade volume ranks lower than China, the USA, and the UAE.
 
• Economic ties are governed by the **India-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IJCEPA)**.

questions.question: DAJGUA Abhiyan which was seen in news in July 2025 is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribal welfare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DAJGUA** stands for **Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan**, a massive mission launched by the **Government of India** to achieve the saturation of critical services in **tribal-majority villages**.
 
• The scheme was formally announced in the **Union Budget 2024-25** and saw significant implementation activity in **July 2025** to improve the **socio-economic** conditions of tribal communities.
 
• The mission aims to cover around **63,000 villages** across **549 districts** and **30 States/UTs**, directly benefiting approximately **5 crore tribal people**.
 
• It adopts a **whole-of-government approach** involving **17 Ministries** to implement **25 interventions** focused on infrastructure, **education**, **healthcare**, and **sustainable livelihood**.
 
• The Abhiyan is named after **Birsa Munda**, the legendary tribal freedom fighter known as **Dharti Aaba** (Father of the Earth), to honor his legacy of **tribal empowerment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**:

 
 
• Acts as the **nodal ministry** for the coordination and monitoring of the **DAJGUA** mission.
 
• Manages other critical initiatives like the **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)** to provide quality middle and high-level education to **ST students**.
 
 
 
• **PM-JANMAN**:
 
 
• Short for **Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan**, it specifically focuses on **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)**.
 
• It addresses **11 critical interventions** including **safe housing**, **clean drinking water**, and **road connectivity** in remote tribal settlements.
 
 
 
• **Food Fortification**:
 
 
• Refers to the process of adding **micronutrients** like **Iron**, **Folic Acid**, and **Vitamin B12** to rice distributed through the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**.
 
• It is a strategic tool to combat **anemia** and **malnutrition**, which are prevalent in **tribal and rural belts**.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission**:
 
 
• A nationwide campaign aimed at eliminating **open defecation** and improving **solid waste management**.
 
• It is categorized into **Gramin** (Rural) and **Urban** components, managed by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** and **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** respectively.

questions.question: What was the name of the Lichchhavi princess married to Chandragupta I?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaradevi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta I**, who ruled from approximately **319 to 335 CE**, was the first powerful sovereign of the **Gupta Dynasty** and adopted the title of **Maharajadhiraja**.
 
• He strengthened his political position and expanded his kingdom's prestige by marrying **Kumaradevi**, a princess belonging to the ancient and influential **Lichchhavi** clan of **Vaishali**.
 
• This matrimonial alliance was so significant that it provided the **Guptas** with the necessary political legitimacy and territorial advantage in the **Magadha** region.
 
• To commemorate this union, **Chandragupta I** issued a unique series of **gold coins**, commonly referred to as the **King-and-Queen type** or **Chandragupta-Kumaradevi** coins.
 
• These coins depict the figures of both the King and the Queen on the obverse, with the name of the **Lichchhavis** (Lichchhavayah) inscribed on the reverse, acknowledging their contribution to the rise of the empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• He was the son of **Chandragupta I** and **Kumaradevi**.
 
• In the **Prayag Prashasti** (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), he is famously described as **Lichchhavi-dauhitra**, meaning the grandson of the **Lichchhavis**.
 
 
 
• **Prabhavati**:
 
 
• **Prabhavati Gupta** was the daughter of **Chandragupta II** and **Kuberanaga**.
 
• She was married into the **Vakataka Dynasty** to King **Rudrasena II** and served as a powerful regent.
 
 
 
• **Nayanika**:
 
 
• Also known as **Naganika**, she was a prominent queen of the **Satavahana Dynasty**.
 
• She was the wife of **Satakarni I** and is noted for the **Naneghat Inscription**.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Era**:
 
 
• The accession of **Chandragupta I** in **319-320 CE** is generally considered the beginning of the **Gupta Era**.

questions.question: In which section of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), plea bargaining has been made time bound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**290**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023** (BNSS), which replaces the **Code of Criminal Procedure** (CrPC), has introduced a specific time limit for filing **plea bargaining** applications to ensure efficiency in the judicial process.
 
• Under **Section 290(1)** of the BNSS, an accused person is permitted to file an application for plea bargaining only within a period of **thirty days** from the date of **framing of charges** by the court.
 
• The application must be filed in the court where the offence is pending trial and must include a description of the case and an **affidavit** affirming that the accused has voluntarily opted for this process without any coercion.
 
• This **time-bound** provision is a significant departure from the previous **CrPC** framework, where no such specific restrictive deadline was explicitly mentioned for the submission of the application after charges were framed.
 
• By imposing a 30-day limit, the legislature aims to prevent the use of plea bargaining as a **delaying tactic** during the later stages of a criminal trial, thereby upholding the principle of **speedy justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plea Bargaining (Chapter XXII)**

 
 
• **Applicability**: It applies to offences that do not carry a punishment of **death**, **imprisonment for life**, or **imprisonment exceeding seven years**.
 
• **Specific Exclusions**: Plea bargaining is strictly prohibited for offences that affect the **socio-economic conditions** of the country or offences committed against a **woman** or a **child below fourteen years** of age.
 
• **Mutually Satisfactory Disposition**: Under **Section 291**, the court provides time for the prosecution, the victim, and the accused to work out a satisfactory disposition of the case, which may include **compensation** to the victim.
 
• **Finality of Judgment**: The judgment delivered by the court under this chapter is **final** and no appeal lies in any court except via a **Special Leave Petition** under **Article 136** or a Writ Petition under **Articles 226 and 227** of the Constitution of India.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who founded the Self-Respect movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Self-Respect Movement** was a significant socio-political movement launched in **1925** by **E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker**, who is popularly and respectfully referred to as **Periyar**.
 
• It originated in the state of **Tamil Nadu** with the primary goal of achieving a society where **backward castes** enjoyed equal human rights and **self-respect**.
 
• **Periyar** initiated this movement after resigning from the **Indian National Congress**, as he believed the party was dominated by **Brahminical interests** and did not sufficiently address **caste-based discrimination**.
 
• The movement strongly advocated for the **abolition of untouchability**, the **empowerment of women**, and the rejection of the **caste hierarchy** and **religious superstitions**.
 
• A hallmark of the movement was the **Self-Respect Marriage** (Swayam Mariyathai Kalyanam), which encouraged unions without **Brahmin priests** or religious rituals to simplify social customs and promote equality.
 
• The ideology of the movement later formed the foundational basis for the **Dravidar Kazhagam** and subsequently influenced the **Dravidian politics** that shaped **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotirao Phule**:

 
 
• A **19th-century** social reformer from **Maharashtra** who founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** in **1873**.
 
• He worked extensively for the **education of women** and the upliftment of the **oppressed classes**, authored **Gulamgiri**, and challenged **Brahminical supremacy**.
 
 
 
• **Shri Narayana Guru**:
 
 
• A spiritual leader and social reformer from **Kerala** who led a reform movement against **casteism**.
 
• He established the **Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam** and gave the famous universal message: **One Caste, One Religion, One God for Mankind**.
 
 
 
• **Ghasidas**:
 
 
• **Guru Ghasidas** was the founder of the **Satnami community** in **Chhattisgarh** during the **18th and 19th centuries**.
 
• He preached the philosophy of **social equality** and monotheism, focusing on the worship of **Satnam** (The True Name) to unite marginalized sections.

questions.question: According to the report "Women in Agribusiness Opportunities and Challenges", what percentage of India's agricultural workforce is constituted by women in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64.4%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled **Women in Agribusiness: Opportunities and Challenges**, jointly prepared by **FICCI** and **PwC India**, highlights the critical demographic shift in the Indian **primary sector**.
 
• According to the findings, women are projected to constitute **64.4%** of the total **agricultural workforce** in India by the year **2025**.
 
• This significant figure is a result of the **feminization of agriculture**, a process where female members of the household take over farming responsibilities as men migrate to urban areas for **non-farm employment**.
 
• The report emphasizes that women are the backbone of the **rural economy**, contributing heavily to **labor-intensive** activities such as sowing, weeding, transplanting, and **livestock management**.
 
• Despite their dominance in numbers, the report identifies that women often lack **legal recognition** as farmers, which hinders their access to **government subsidies** and **support schemes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agribusiness Landscape:**

 
 
• The report notes that while **women participation** is high in production, it remains significantly lower in **value-added segments** like processing, logistics, and **agri-tech leadership**.
 
• Closing the **gender gap** in agriculture could potentially increase **farm yields** by **20% to 30%**, fostering greater **food security**.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Barriers:**
 
 
• Key challenges cited include a lack of **land titles**, limited access to **institutional credit**, and the **digital divide** in rural connectivity.
 
• Societal norms frequently restrict women from participating in **agricultural markets** (Mandis), limiting their **income potential**.
 
 
 
• **Policy Focus:**
 
 
• To empower women farmers, the report suggests strengthening **Women Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)** and providing **gender-friendly machinery** to reduce **physical drudgery**.
 
• Encouraging **financial literacy** and **entrepreneurial training** is essential for transitioning women from laborers to **agri-entrepreneurs**.

questions.question: What is the rank of Anna University in the Times Higher Education (THE) Asia Rankings 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**111**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anna University**, a premier technical institution located in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**, has achieved a significant milestone by securing the **111th** position in the **Times Higher Education (THE) Asia University Rankings**.
 
• This ranking represents a major leap for the university, which was previously positioned in the **201–250** band in the preceding evaluation cycle, reflecting rapid improvements in its academic and research output.
 
• The **THE Asia University Rankings** utilize 18 rigorous performance indicators to assess institutions across five main pillars: **Teaching**, **Research Environment**, **Research Quality**, **International Outlook**, and **Industry** connections.
 
• The university's elevation to rank **111** is largely attributed to its high scores in **Research Quality**, which measures citation impact and research excellence, as well as its strong **Industry Income**, indicating successful knowledge transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Times Higher Education (THE) Rankings**

 
 
• The **THE Asia University Rankings** focus specifically on the performance of universities across the **Asian continent**, providing a benchmark for educational excellence in the region.
 
• The 2024-2025 ranking cycle saw **India** emerge as the **second-most represented nation** with over **90 institutions** making the list, trailing only **China**.
 
 
 
• **Leading Indian Institutions**
 
 
• The **Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bangalore** continues to lead the Indian contingent, maintaining its status in the top tier of Asian universities.
 
• Other notable performers alongside **Anna University** include various **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)** and private research universities, showcasing a diversified growth in the **Indian Higher Education** sector.
 
 
 
• **Methodology and Impact**
 
 
• The **Research Quality** pillar, accounting for **30%** of the total weightage, is a critical factor where Indian technical universities like **Anna University** have shown substantial growth.
 
• Global rankings like these influence **International Student** recruitment, **Faculty Collaboration**, and government funding under schemes like the **Institution of Eminence (IoE)**.
